practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient (singleton) per process and do not create a new client per request; cache/connect once and share the client across handlers.
practices.prior_belief: Always create and reuse a single MongoClient instance per process (or per container) instead of creating a new client per request; configure maxPoolSize to match expected concurrency (e.g., maxPoolSize=100) and set sensible timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS).

practices.practice: Keep the DocumentDB connection string and credentials out of source control: read them from environment variables or retrieve from Azure Key Vault at runtime instead of committing secrets to files.
practices.prior_belief: Keep the DocumentDB/MongoDB connection string/credentials out of source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (or individual creds) from environment variables and/or store them in Azure Key Vault and fetch at runtime rather than writing secrets to files.

practices.practice: Always use TLS for connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production (tls=true and validate server certificates).
practices.prior_belief: Enable TLS/SSL for connections and validate server certificates (tls=true / ssl=true and tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false) to prevent MITM: ensure the driver connection string includes the required TLS parameters used by the cluster.

practices.practice: Use least-privilege credentials and prefer Microsoft Entra ID / RBAC and per-application users instead of using admin/root credentials in the app.
practices.prior_belief: Grant least-privilege credentials: create a DB user/account with just the required roles (read on sales/lead_time collections, readWrite on purchase_orders) rather than using an admin/root credential in the app.

practices.practice: Model time-series-like sales velocity as compact summaries (one document per SKU or SKU+store with bounded-size history or pre-aggregated summaries) and store raw events separately if needed for reprocessing.
practices.prior_belief: Model time-series-like sales velocity as one compact document per SKU (or per SKU+store) containing a bounded-size rolling window array or a summarized histogram rather than an unbounded transaction collection; if raw events are needed, store them separately and aggregate into summaries for forecasting queries.

practices.practice: Enforce idempotency for purchase orders with a unique index (for example on product_id + period + supplier_id or an order_reference) and use upsert or conditional writes to avoid duplicate orders from concurrent agents.
practices.prior_belief: Add a unique index (or unique field constraint) to enforce idempotency for purchase orders (for example unique compound index on product_id + period + supplier_id or a unique order_reference) and use upsert with that filter to avoid duplicate orders from the orchestrator agent.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral agent-memory documents (index a Date field with expireAfterSeconds) but ensure the field is a Date and understand expiration is not instantaneous (~60s background sweeper).
practices.prior_belief: Create TTL indexes for ephemeral agent memory documents (shared agent memory) to automatically expire them after the retention window (e.g., createIndex({last_updated:1}, {expireAfterSeconds: 86400})).

practices.practice: Index every field used as a filter or sort key in production queries and design compound indexes using ESR (Equality → Sort → Range) to avoid COLLSCAN and reduce query costs.
practices.prior_belief: Index all fields used as filters or sort keys in production queries: at minimum index product_id, last_sale_date, supplier_id and any compound combinations used by the forecast or supplier selection queries to avoid collection scans.

practices.practice: Store fixed-length numeric embeddings in a dedicated field and create a vector index whose dimensions and similarity exactly match the model (e.g., createIndex({embedding: 'cosmosSearch'}, {cosmosSearchOptions:{kind:'vector-diskann',dimensions:1536,similarity:'COS'}})).
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, store fixed-length float32 arrays in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: [f1, f2, ...]) and create a vector index specifying the correct dimension and metric (L2/cosine) so nearest-neighbor queries are efficient rather than doing an $where or application-side scan.

practices.practice: When building a vector index, pick the engine (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) appropriate to scale and tune parameters (maxDegree, lBuild) and tune query-time parameters (lSearch / ef) to trade recall vs latency; rebuild the index if you change embedding dimensions or similarity.
practices.prior_belief: When creating a vector index, tune indexing parameters (index type such as hnsw or ivf, m and efConstruction for HNSW, nlists for IVF) and set ef (or efSearch) at query time to trade accuracy vs latency; persist these parameters as part of DB provisioning documentation.

practices.practice: Limit projection to only the fields the agent needs (use find(..., projection) or aggregation $project) to reduce network transfer and serialization costs, especially when reading embeddings or large histories.
practices.prior_belief: Limit projection in queries to only the fields required by the agent (use find(..., projection={fields}) or aggregation $project) to reduce network transfer and deserialization costs when reading embeddings or large histories.

practices.practice: Compute rollups and sales-velocity metrics server-side with aggregation pipelines instead of fetching large raw datasets, and create indexes that support the pipeline pattern (match → sort → group).
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side aggregation pipelines (aggregation framework) to compute rollups and sales-velocity metrics instead of pulling large raw datasets into the app for forecasting; create indexes that support these pipeline stages (match->sort->group).

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network/5xx errors and limit retry budget; use idempotent operations (e.g., upsert with a unique key) so retries do not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff for transient network and 5xx errors and limit total retry budget; use idempotent operations (e.g., upsert with unique key) so retries do not create duplicates.

practices.practice: When strong ordering or causal guarantees are required, prefer explicit DB-level consistency controls (readConcern / writeConcern / session options) where supported and make critical writes durable before downstream actions; verify the service-level mapping for Azure DocumentDB before relying on specific readConcern/writeConcern semantics.
practices.prior_belief: Prefer causally consistent reads or explicit readConcern and writeConcern for workflows that require strong ordering (for example, make the orchestrator confirm a write is majority-committed before triggering supplier notifications); set readConcern='local' or 'majority' and writeConcern appropriately for required durability.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB readConcern writeConcern causal consistency (searched via Microsoft docs)

practices.practice: Provision appropriate compute/throughput (pick suitable cluster tier and storage) and use autoscale/scale decisions based on compute-tier IO caps; batch large concurrent writes and use bulkWrite with ordered:false where idempotency permits to avoid saturating the DB.
practices.prior_belief: Provision collections with appropriate throughput/compute (provisioned RU/s or equivalent) and use autoscale if available; avoid saturating the DB with large bulk writes from concurrent agents—batch writes and use bulkWrite with ordered:false where idempotency permits.
practices.how_found: documentdb-azure-deployment -> deployment tier and sizing guidance; documentdb-storage

practices.practice: Keep purchase-order documents small and store large or static supplier metadata separately (reference by ID) to keep hot collections small and efficient to index and query.
practices.prior_belief: When writing purchase orders, write small documents and store large static supplier metadata separately (supplier contact info, terms) referenced by ID to keep hot collections small and indexed.

practices.practice: Use change streams (the service supports change streams) or a lightweight notification mechanism to trigger agents instead of frequent polling; Azure DocumentDB exposes change streams and an Azure Functions trigger for them.
practices.prior_belief: Use change streams or a lightweight notification mechanism (if supported) to trigger re-evaluation by agents instead of frequent polling; if change streams are unavailable, schedule batched polling with backoff and lastProcessedTimestamp checkpoints.
practices.how_found: Azure Learn: Change streams in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Capture and log query performance: enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs, use explain('executionStats') for hot queries and alert on high docsExamined / CPU / IOPS to drive index and query fixes.
practices.prior_belief: Capture and log query performance: use explain() to verify that key queries (sales velocity aggregation, supplier selection, vector nearest-neighbor) use the intended indexes and avoid COLLSCAN; record and act on slow query alerts.

practices.practice: For latency-sensitive vector nearest-neighbor lookups, include a short pre-filter (e.g., category or product_type) in the vector search query to reduce the candidate set and improve latency and accuracy.
practices.prior_belief: For latency-sensitive vector nearest-neighbor lookups, store a short pre-filter (e.g., category, product_type) and include it in the vector search query to reduce the candidate set and improve latency/accuracy.
practices.how_found: documentdb-vector-search -> vector-knn-query (recommendation to combine with pre-filters)

practices.practice: Validate inputs in the application and use the service's JSON schema validation ($jsonSchema) to catch malformed documents early; store schemaVersion to support migrations.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid server-side schema assumptions: validate inputs in the application (schema, embedding dimension, numeric ranges) and add JSON schema validation or triggers if the DB supports them to catch malformed documents early.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB does not support retryable multi-document writes; connection strings returned by the service include retryWrites=false and drivers should not assume retryable-writes semantics.
